entries.title: He Binds What Is Hurt

entries.scene_uniqueness: Tending an already found hurt sheep differs in purpose and action from existing carrying, seeking, calling, following, wolf defense and pit rescue images.
entries.proposed_caption: The Shepherd tends a hurt sheep with patient hands. Ezekiel 34:11–16 joins the promise to seek the lost with the promise to strengthen and bind what is hurt.

entries.prompt: Create a close, natural landscape view of a shallow rural spring pool with six sheep. entries.proposed_caption: The bow is broken and the spear lies still beside a charred wheel. Psalm 46:6–11 turns from nations in turmoil toward the Lord who makes wars cease.
entries.prompt: Create one restrained photographic still life inspired by Psalm 46:6–11, especially verses 8–10. On bare ancient-looking earth lie a single broken wooden bow with slack string, one splintered spear shaft with an intact dull metal point directed away from the viewer, and part of a charred wooden chariot wheel. All objects are inert and plainly unusable; no people, bodies, blood, active fire, combat, burning buildings or triumphal flags. Soft morning daylight reveals weathered wood and quiet empty space beyond. Use plausible simple ancient materials without naming an archaeological site, nation, date or recovered artifact. This is visual reflection on the psalm’s poetry, not a purported photograph of a recorded battlefield, not a modern war scene and not a fantasy weapons poster. Create one new 1536x1024 landscape image with convincing live-action photographic clarity, natural wood, metal and earth textures, coherent object construction and physically plausible light. Keep all three inert objects within generous 3:2 margins. No people, painting, CGI, glamour, halos, writing, watermark or collage.
